Your expedition: DevOps at Polarsteps

One person, the whole platform.

Polarsteps helps 23+ million travellers plan, track and relive their trips, and all of it runs on our infrastructure. As our DevOps Engineer, you’ll be the main point of contact for that infrastructure. You’ll work alongside our Platform team and support all 8 of our engineering teams, so everyone can ship with confidence.

There’s plenty of room to bring your own ideas and improve how we work, with a supportive team around you to figure things out together. If you enjoy being hands-on, setting up good processes and helping others make the right technical choices, this is your kind of adventure.

Our ambition is big. We want our infrastructure ready for 100 million+ users, built efficiently in both cost and resources.

Your itinerary

What your journey at Polarsteps will look like day-to-day:

You will:

  • Report to Simeon, our Lead Backend Engineer, and work closely with our Platform team (Youri, William, Paco, Jimmy, Florian and Ledio) and team leads across Engineering.

  • Spot bottlenecks in our architecture and scaling, both for users and for developer experience. You’ll create and execute a plan with Engineering and other stakeholders.

  • Review, improve and maintain our observability, monitoring and alerting.

  • Manage and respond to incidents, and keep our infrastructure and troubleshooting documentation up to date.

  • Strengthen platform security and privacy, working alongside our external security lead.

  • Lead initiatives like rolling out company-wide SSO and managing our VPN.

  • You use AI tools like Claude Code, MCP servers and AI-assisted observability (e.g. Datadog) as a daily part of your workflow, from debugging incidents and infrastructure issues to writing and reviewing code.

  • Support our Data team with the infrastructure behind our analytics stack.

The equipment in your backpack

What we’re hoping you’ll bring with you:

  • 5+ years as a DevOps Engineer, SRE or Platform Engineer.

  • Experience automating infrastructure and processes on AWS.

  • Fluency in shell scripting, Python and Terraform / OpenTofu.

  • Comfort making changes to backend code when automation calls for it.

  • A pragmatic mindset: you know when to cut corners and when to build something that lasts.

  • Clear communication with technical and non-technical people, helping them reach decisions on complex trade-offs.

  • Autonomy and a collaborative nature. You’re happy setting up your own processes while working with everyone.

Bonus points if you’ve worked with Nix, Kubernetes, ArgoCD or ECS, RabbitMQ, or TypeScript on the frontend ✨

1st class extras

  • Salary range: Between EUR 84.000 and 99.000 gross per year incl 8% holiday allowance (based on 40 hours/week). Where you land in the range depends on your experience and skills, to be evaluated during the interview process.

  • Hybrid working. Split your time between the office and your home, as you see fit.

  • The option to switch up your zoom background by working from another country for up to 8 weeks a year.

  • A personal development budget for that curious mind of yours!

As our next Senior Software Engineer in Trust & Safety, you'll own the systems that decide how tradespeople are checked, how reviews are processed and how our marketplace stays honest at scale. You'll work alongside the vetting and reviews teams, who are on the front line of trust, and build the infrastructure that lets them work with confidence. When something breaks in production, you'll lead the response. When something looks brittle at design time, you'll say so.

The job, unfiltered:

  • Own and evolve the systems behind how tradespeople are verified, how reviews flow through our platform and how content is moderated.

  • Lead the response when things break: read distributed traces, correlate logs across services and find the cause, not just the symptom.

  • Design event-driven workflows that are reliable by default: idempotent, retryable, with dead-letter handling that doesn't need a 2am wake-up to unpick.

  • Work directly with the vetting and reviews teams to understand what trust means day to day, then build systems that hold up to it.

  • Tighten the operational seams: better monitoring, clearer alerting, locked-down auth and outbox patterns that keep data consistent.

The fit:

  • Strong TypeScript. You're comfortable owning a service end to end, from schema to deployment.

  • Fastify or a similar Node.js framework, and enough HTTP know-how that it rarely surprises you.

  • Event-driven instincts: you know what idempotency means in practice and why the outbox pattern exists.

  • Full-stack comfort, Next.js included. You ship the frontend as happily as the service behind it.

  • Datadog fluency (APM traces, log search, metric queries), SQL for diagnostics during an incident, and GCP basics such as Pub/Sub backlogs and DLQs.

  • Experience leading production incidents, not just being in them. You communicate clearly under pressure and drive to a fix.

  • An eye for systemic problems at review time, not at post-mortem time, and a habit of making the people around you better.

  • Regular use of AI tools like Cursor or Claude Code, and a keen interest in helping the team get more out of them.

This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture

AI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there; knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.

Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist, even before the next generation arrives. That is the opportunity we are building around.

We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the result against agreed quality standards. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the right combination for the task.

Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.

Our founder brings considerable drive, a hands-on approach and a strong sense of urgency to building the company. Backed by Atlantic at pre-seed, we are growing the engineering team to bring the product into production, with people already waiting to use it.

About the Role

As one of our first platform engineers, you will build the foundations that every product feature depends on: the gateway and router, usage and billing systems, customer key management and the European infrastructure underneath.

Much of that platform is still taking shape. Working directly with the founder, CTO and founding AI engineer, you will help turn early architectural decisions into systems that remain reliable as the product grows.

You will take capabilities from design through to production, thinking through their APIs, failure modes, deployment, observability and ongoing operation. In a team this small, building and running the system belong together. You will also work alongside our founding AI engineer on evals, embeddings and open-weight model serving, bringing platform engineering depth to the ML side of the product.

Agentic engineering is central to how we work. You will operate in an agentic way by default, using coding agents as a core part of how you design, build, test and ship software. You'll develop the harnesses and workflows that allow you to delegate and parallelise work effectively, increasing what a small engineering team can deliver. This requires strong coding fundamentals and the judgement to review, challenge and take responsibility for everything that reaches production.

There is a lot to build and an ambitious timeline ahead. We work with intensity, move quickly from decisions to execution and value people who take initiative and see things through.

What You’ll Work On

Your first area of ownership will depend on your strengths and our priorities. From there, you will contribute across the platform as it develops.

  • Gateway and routing: build a consistent API across model providers, with reliable streaming, fallbacks and safe handling of retries and provider errors.

  • Agentic engineering workflows: build and refine the harnesses, tooling and workflows that enable coding agents to work effectively across the development lifecycle, from implementation and testing to debugging and deployment.

  • Cost optimisation: develop caching, history compression and model selection, measuring savings while keeping estimated costs distinct from actual spend.

  • Usage and billing: build accurate accounting for model calls, usage reports, plan entitlements and invoice reconciliation.

  • Agent infrastructure and integrations: support tool calls, cost limits, human approvals and runs that can recover safely from interruptions, alongside connectors for services such as Gmail, Slack and calendars.

  • Tenancy and secrets: maintain workspace isolation, secure authentication and encrypted customer key management.

  • European infrastructure and model serving: build and operate our cloud infrastructure, including the GPU capacity used to serve open-weight models.

  • Production reliability: make systems observable, migrations reversible and releases safe, with tests that protect data integrity and logs that keep customer content and secrets private.

The platform will evolve quickly. You will need to move comfortably between improving what exists and learning enough about a new problem to build the next piece well.

Our Stack

Our backend is built in Python, with a TypeScript frontend in a shared monorepo.

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic and LiteLLM.

  • Data and queues: Postgres with row-level security and pgvector, Redis and arq.

  • Frontend: Next.js, React and TypeScript.

  • Cloud and infrastructure: Scaleway, Terraform and Kubernetes for GPU workloads.

  • Auth and secrets: Zitadel, Secret Manager and KMS.

  • Observability and testing: OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Sentry, pytest and testcontainers, alongside frontend testing tools.

You should be comfortable with the core backend technologies and ready to learn the rest as the work requires.

Astronomer empowers data teams to bring mission-critical software, analytics, and AI to life and is the company behind Astro, the industry-leading unified DataOps platform powered by Apache Airflow®. Astro accelerates building reliable data products that unlock insights, unleash AI value, and powers data-driven applications. Trusted by more than 800 of the world's leading enterprises, Astronomer lets businesses do more with their data. To learn more, visit www.astronomer.io.

About this role

Astronomer’s products run on a complex, multi-cloud platform — and the scalability, and operational maturity of that platform is what we’re actively investing in. The work ahead on our Platform team isn’t about managing data or curating pipelines; it’s about building the foundational systems that everything else runs on — the kind of systems where the failure modes matter, the latency budgets are real, and getting it wrong has visible consequences for hundreds of enterprise customers.

We’re looking for a Staff+-level engineer who has built production platform systems at scale before — not just consumed them. You’ve designed systems under load, reasoned carefully about failure, and made your colleagues’ lives better by giving them something solid and well-understood to build on top of. You write strategy documents and then write the code that proves them out. You’ve been the person who made the call, and lived with the consequences.

This is a foundational role at a consequential moment: your work will directly shape what Astronomer’s products — Astro, Observe, and our IDE — are capable of over the next several years.

What you get to do

Astronomer has a healthy and complex infrastructure estate spanning multiple cloud providers, a mix of managed and self-hosted systems, and an increasingly ambitious set of requirements as our products evolve. We have a clear sense of where we need to go; we need the right person to figure out how to get there and then go build it.

This is very much a technical role — you’ll be just as involved in building these systems as in specifying and designing them. We’re not looking for someone to write strategy documents; we’re looking for someone who writes the strategy and the code, and who has done exactly that before at scale.

  • Blaze a Trail: Own and develop our platform infrastructure strategy, with the sponsorship and responsibility to match. Map out what we need, make the calls, and own the outcomes.

  • Be an Owner: Be directly involved in deciding what we work on and how we work on it. Make promises, and keep them.

  • Do Sensible Things: Make principled build vs. buy assessments and advocate for the right tools for the right job — not the fashionable ones, not the ones already in the estate just because they’re there.

  • Garage Door Open: Create and maintain comprehensive internal documentation and decision records for systems and processes. Participate in architectural forums and make principled, open decisions that the rest of the organisation can learn from and hold us to.

What you bring to the role

  • Distributed systems depth, grounded in practice. You have a solid working model of how production systems fail — consistency and availability tradeoffs, failure cascades, backpressure, graceful degradation. You can draw the diagram, explain the failure modes at each node, and make a reasoned argument for which ones actually matter in a given context. NALSD thinking is how you naturally approach a new system design.

  • Kubernetes at operator depth. You know what happens inside the scheduler and the control loop when things go wrong, because you’ve been there. You’ve operated clusters under real load, not just deployed workloads onto them.

  • Strong Go proficiency. The platform team writes production Go. You should be fluent: you’ve built and shipped systems in it, and you have opinions about what good Go looks like.

  • Multi-cloud experience, not just multi-cloud exposure. You’ve made considered architectural decisions across AWS, GCP, and/or Azure — not just consumed managed services, but evaluated tradeoffs between them and lived with those decisions in production.

  • Experience defining requirements and driving technology choices across an engineering organization. You’ve been the person in the room who frames the decision correctly, not just the one who executes it.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. You can write a design doc that changes minds, and a postmortem that makes the organisation smarter. You’ve worked effectively in a globally-distributed team.

    The estimated total compensation for this role ranges from €140,000 - €215,000, along with an equity component and a comprehensive benefits package. This range is merely an estimate, and the width of the range reflects willingness to consider candidates with broad prior seniority. Actual compensation may deviate from this range based on skills, experience, and qualifications.

Bonus points if you have

  • Experience with storage primitives at the system level — you’ve reasoned about when to reach for a relational store vs. an object store vs. something else, and you have real opinions informed by real failures.

  • Experience working on a SaaS/PaaS product across multiple cloud providers.

  • Familiarity with Apache Airflow or workflow orchestration systems.

We are a certified B Corporation, upholding the belief that businesses should have a positive impact on society.

✨ Our values

Our values guide our approach to work and are at the heart of our recruitment process. To join our team, we look for individuals who value:

  • Excellence: We think that every detail counts, and we place great importance on the quality of our deliverables.

  • Trust: We are passionate, committed, and free to act with autonomy.

  • Happiness at work: We enjoy looking on the bright side and we share our enthusiasm with our colleagues and clients.

🤝 The team

You will join our Global MidMarket Customer Success team, a group of Customer Success Managers who each own a broad, evolving portfolio of mid-market accounts. While the function operates globally, this specific opening is dedicated to the EMEA & APAC regions

Based in Paris, you will work closely with 2 Mid-Market CSMs (1 in London, 1 in NYC) and 1 Scale Ops Manager (Paris). Matthieu, Head of Scale CSM and your manager, based in Paris, will support you in achieving your goals. You will also be part of a global Customer Success community across our international offices.

Here is what the Go-To-Market organization looks like at UpSlide:

  • Account Executives: Prospect, acquire new business acquisition and expand existing accounts

  • Consultants: Lead implementation projects, deliver client training, and ensure successful deployment

  • Customer Success Managers: Own a portfolio of accounts end-to-end, driving retention, renewal signing, expansion within existing entities, value realization, and long-term account growth. Split between Enterprise CSMs, who build deep, tailored relationships with a small number of strategic accounts, and Mid-Market CSMs, who manage a larger book of accounts with a focus on speed and ROI, acting where and when it counts

  • Support Engineers: Resolve day-to-day technical questions and issues, and ensure a smooth customer experience

🖋️ Your responsibilities

As a Mid-Market Customer Success Manager, you will own a broad portfolio of Mid-Market accounts end-to-end. Working at pace and using usage data and account signals to prioritize your day, you will make sure your accounts renew, stay healthy, and grow, spotting upsell/expand opportunities as proactively as you spot churn risk, and owning both through to close.

This is a role for someone energized by volume and by building repeatable, data-driven ways of working across a large book of business, without losing the client-first mindset that drives portfolio growth.

Portfolio Ownership & Signal-Driven Execution (60%)

Own the business performance and KPIs of a large portfolio of Mid-Market accounts, and take individual accountability for contributing to team and company targets:

  • Own your portfolio's KPIs (usage, renewal rate, NRR, churn) end to end with a hunter/rescuer mindset: moving fast to capture opportunity, and stepping in decisively when an account is at risk

  • Structure your coverage around two core touchpoints, kickoff and renewal, complemented by additional touchpoints where and when the data calls for it

  • Continuously monitor usage data, health scores, and other signals to prioritize your day and catch risk or opportunity early

  • React quickly and decisively on negative signals to protect the account, and on positive signals to capture upsell potential

  • Judge, account by account, how much time and effort a situation deserves, and adjust your touchpoint cadence accordingly - guided increasingly by shared scoring and playbooks as the Scale motion matures

Product & Industry Expertise (20%)

Build broad product and industry expertise to support adoption at scale, rather than deep knowledge of any single client:

  • Develop a strong understanding of UpSlide's product and of the industries your portfolio operates in

  • Contribute to adoption initiatives such as webinars and open office hours, sharing your expertise across the client base

Scale Motion Optimization (10%)

Bring a critical eye to how the Mid-Market motion runs, and help make it faster and more effective:

  • Share structured feedback on where automation and process changes can save time

  • Suggest and help build content that increases client engagement and adoption

  • Work closely with the Scale Ops Manager and the Head of Scale to turn feedback into concrete improvements

Cross-functional Collaboration (10%)

Stay connected to the teams around your portfolio, notably those handling first-line requests:

  • Sync regularly with Support and Sales Admin, who own level 1 requests and escalate to you when needed

  • Partner with Sales on expansion opportunities that require broader support

To work on these tasks, you will mainly use the following tools: Microsoft Office, UpSlide, Salesforce, Gong, PowerBI, Notion (or local equivalents).

⚡ Your goals

What you'll be assessed on:

  • Net Revenue Retention (NRR)

  • Churn

  • Upsell / Expansion contribution

  • CRM data quality and forecast accuracy


You are a great fit if you have:

  • 2/3+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or a related client-facing/revenue role in a B2B environment

  • Proven experience managing renewals and churn across a portfolio of accounts, with the confidence to handle difficult conversations (renegotiation, dissatisfaction) as needed

  • Proven ability to identify and close expansion/upsell opportunities, with a hunter mindset and a strong ROI orientation

  • Experience autonomously managing a sizeable portfolio, ideally including Mid-Market accounts

  • A structured, analytical approach to account planning at volume, using data to prioritize a broad book of business and anticipate risk

  • Operational rigor: accurate CRM data, reliable follow-up, dependable forecasting

  • Excellent written and verbal communication in French and English

  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, international environment

We’d love it if you have:

  • Experience with analytics / BI tools (PowerBI or equivalent)

  • Advanced negotiation skills

  • Knowledge of the financial services / professional services sector

  • Familiarity with SaaS metrics (ARR, NRR, churn, forecasting) and reporting to leadership

✨ If you don’t tick all the boxes but you think you’d be a great fit, please apply and tell us why.

Recruitment process

  1. Screening call with a Talent Acquisition Specialist: A conversation to walk through your experience, motivation, and fit for the role.

  2. Interview with your future manager or their peer: A deeper dive into your Customer Success experience and approach to account management.

  3. Case study + team-meet: A live exercise reflecting real challenges of the role, followed by a conversation with members of the wider team.

  4. Final conversation with leadership: A closing discussion to align on ambition, expectations, and next steps.

🚀 We'll conduct a reference check to learn how to help you thrive. On average, our process lasts 3 weeks.

What we offer

Our engineering ways of working:

  • Our Product and Engineering organisation is structured into four tribes: Custody, Accounts, Experience, and Cloud & Security. Each tribe contains multiple autonomous squads, with clear full ownership over specific product domains.

Über die Position

Gestalte mit uns die digitale Infrastruktur des europäischen Gartenbaus

Connected Growers entwickelt June  - die Plattform, über die Erzeuger, B2B Käufer und Vermarkter effizient zusammenarbeiten. Wir ersetzen fragmentierte Prozesse durch moderne Software und schaffen eine gemeinsame digitale Infrastruktur für eine ganze Branche.

Dafür suchen wir Verstärkung als Tech Lead Marketplace Experience (m/w/d), um nicht nur Software zu entwickeln, sondern ein Team aufzubauen, technische Verantwortung zu übernehmen und gemeinsam mit dem Produkt-Team die Zukunft unserer Plattform zu gestalten.

Deine Rolle bei June

Als Tech Lead Grower Marketplace Experience (m/w/d) verantwortest du die technische Entwicklung unseres Marketplace und der dazugehörigen Services. Du berichtest direkt an unsere CTO Anna.

Du baust einen neuen Engineering Squad von Grund auf auf und übernimmst die technische und fachliche Verantwortung für einen der kommerziell wichtigsten Bereiche von June. Es geht nicht nur darum, gute Software zu bauen: Du setzt technische Richtung, triffst Entscheidungen unter Unsicherheit, entwickelst Menschen, und prägst die Kultur deines Squads. Du sorgst gemeinsam mit dem Produkt-Team dafür, dass wir Funktionen entwickeln, die für unsere Kunden messbaren Mehrwert schaffen.

Wir geben dir den Kontext und den Freiraum, den du brauchst, um deinen Bereich eigenständig zu führen. Im Gegenzug erwarten wir, dass du Verantwortung übernimmst, Entscheidungen triffst und auch für ihre Konsequenzen einstehst – in einem dynamischen Umfeld, in dem sich Prioritäten verändern und Informationen nicht immer vollständig vorliegen.

Du bist kein klassischer People Manager. Du führst über technische Tiefe, Klarheit, Entscheidungen und Vertrauen. Du bleibst hands-on im Code, ohne zum technischen Bottleneck zu werden, triffst Architekturentscheidungen und unterstützt dein Team dabei, gemeinsam hochwertige Software zu entwickeln.

Unser Marketplace basiert auf dem Spryker Commerce OS. Du entwickelst ein klares Verständnis dafür, wann wir innerhalb der Spryker-Konventionen arbeiten, wann wir erweitern und wann eine individuelle Lösung sinnvoll ist. Dabei behältst du immer die langfristige Wartbarkeit und Erweiterbarkeit unserer Plattform im Blick.


Anforderungen

Was du mitbringst

  • Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung als Tech Lead oder Senior Engineer in Web- und E-Commerce-Anwendungen sowie fundierte praktische Erfahrung mit PHP und Spryker Commerce OS und weißt, wann du innerhalb der Spryker-Konventionen arbeitest, erweiterst oder bewusst davon abweichst.

  • Du bringst Erfahrung mit API- bzw. Spec-first-Entwicklung sowie mit AWS-Cloud-Infrastrukturen, modernen Deployment-Prozessen und Monitoring mit.

  • Du hast bereits Erfahrung im Teamaufbau und weißt, worauf es ankommt.

  • Du hast Verständnis, Interesse und Lust an Produktentwicklung (Software) und Teamentwicklung (Menschen).

  • Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, kommunizierst klar, hast hohe Qualitätsansprüche und sprichst fließend Deutsch sowie sehr gutes Englisch.

Das wäre ein Plus

  • Gute Kenntnisse in TypeScript.

  • Erfahrung mit ERP-, Warehouse- oder Commerce-Systemen.

  • Erfahrung mit komplexen Order-, Pricing- oder Inventory/Catalogue-Prozessen.

  • Erfahrung in einem Startup oder schnell wachsenden Technologieunternehmen.


Aufgabenbereich

Was du bei uns bewegst

  • Du verantwortest Architektur, technische Qualität und Weiterentwicklung des Marketplace und seiner Services.

  • Du baust dein Squad auf, entwickelst deine Teammitglieder weiter und schaffst eine Kultur aus Ownership, Pragmatismus und kontinuierlichem Lernen.

  • Du entwickelst eine klare technische Strategie für den Produktbereich Marketplace Experience und triffst bewusste Entscheidungen darüber, wie wir Spryker einsetzen und erweitern.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit dem Produkt-Team zusammen und übersetzt die Bedürfnisse unserer Käufer und Verkäufer in nachhaltige technische Lösungen..

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass dein Team Software kontinuierlich, sicher und zuverlässig ausliefert – von der technischen Spezifikation und Architektur über API-Design und Entwicklung bis hin zu Betrieb, Incident Management und kontinuierlicher Verbesserung.

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung für Performance, Stabilität, Security und Compliance und stellst sicher, dass technische Risiken früh erkannt, bewertet und bewusst adressiert werden.

  • Du nutzt AI selbstverständlich im Engineering-Alltag und hilfst deinem Team dabei, AI sinnvoll und verantwortungsvoll für Entwicklung, Testing, Dokumentation und Code Reviews einzusetzen.

So arbeiten wir

Unsere Teams verantworten ihren Produktbereich komplett: Architektur, API-Design, Entwicklung, Betrieb, Incidents, Security, Compliance. Die kommerziellen KPIs gehören dazu.

Wir reden mit Kunden, fahren zu ihnen raus, testen unsere Lösungen dort im Betrieb. Verantwortung endet nicht am Merge-Button.


Die Perspektive

Was dich erwartet

  • Du baust etwas auf, statt ein bestehendes Team zu verwalten.

  • Du bekommst einen klar abgegrenzten Verantwortungsbereich und die Freiheit, ihn zu gestalten.

  • Du arbeitest direkt mit CTO und Product Manager und kannst technische, produktbezogene, kulturprägende und kommerzielle Entscheidungen tatsächlich beeinflussen.

  • Du siehst die Konsequenzen deiner Entscheidungen unmittelbar – im Produkt, im Team und im Geschäft.

  • Hybrides Arbeiten in unserem Büro in Köln sowie regelmäßige Besuche bei Kund*innen, Gärtner*innen und Partner*innen vor Ort



Diese Stellenbeschreibung ist bewusst meinungsstark und setzt hohe Standards. Wir suchen nicht den perfekten Lebenslauf, sondern Menschen, die bei Connected Growers glücklich werden. Wenn du nicht alle formalen Kriterien erfüllst, dich aber in der Art, wie wir arbeiten und führen, wiedererkennst, freuen wir uns trotzdem über deine Bewerbung. Was dir an einzelnen Punkten noch fehlt, können wir gemeinsam entwickeln – entscheidend ist, dass du das Mindset und die Bereitschaft mitbringst, in diese Rolle hineinzuwachsen.

Hinweis: Die Stelle wird zunächst über BridgeMaker besetzt und im weiteren Verlauf zu Connected Growers überführt.

Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time https://cardog.app/careers

We're the system of record for the Canadian vehicle: raw automotive data turned into facts that can be checked. Our open-source VIN decoder sits underneath a government vehicle registry.

Some of what's interesting:

- A government registry, a manufacturer's own filing, a listing site and an insurance record will describe the same truck four different ways, and nothing in any of those files says they're the same truck. Reconciling that, for every vehicle in the country, in a way that holds up when a regulator asks how you know, is most of the data work.

- Seventeen characters on a door frame encode manufacturer, plant, model year and build attributes — badly, inconsistently, and differently per manufacturer. Public reference data covers some of it. The rest gets worked out from filings, recall documents, and patterns inferred across millions of vehicles.

- We read vehicles directly over OBD-II now. Forty modules answered on a recent Hyundai, each reporting its own part number and installed software version. Nothing downstream of the VIN moves when a module is reflashed, so no registration, history report or dealer system knows what software is actually in a car.

Hiring: VIN Decode Engineer, Data Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, Founding Engineer (dealer platform). TypeScript, Postgres, Cloudflare Workers.

Full descriptions and apply: https://cardog.app/careers
